[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
'''Philip Glasco''', described as ''junior'' or ''the younger'', was a watchmaker in Christ-church-lane, Dublin. His birth and parents have not been established by an inspected birth or family record.

An original death column published on 28 September 1765 names the unnamed wife of Mr. Philip Glasco, junior, watchmaker in Christ-church-lane. The designation, trade and address strongly support the younger watchmaker’s identity. The notice does not give his wife’s forename or maiden surname; do not identify that wife as Teresa Plunkett.<ref name="Wife 1765">''The Public Register, or, Freeman’s Journal'', 28 September 1765, p.3, [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050029120/ original scan], inspected in the project’s 4 October 2026 review. The Ireland Old News extraction of Faulkner’s 28 September issue reports the wife’s death under 24 September; publication and event dates remain distinct.</ref>

The original marriage column published on 20 September 1768 names Mr. Phil. Glasco the younger, watchmaker of Christ-church-lane, and Miss Teresa Plunkett of Church-street.<ref name="Marriage 1768">''The Public Register, or, Freeman’s Journal'', 20 September 1768, p.3, [https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050148115/ original scan], inspected 4 October 2026.</ref> The Public Gazetteer extraction dated 17 September 1768 reports the same named couple. These are retained newspaper dates, not a newly proved exact ceremony date.<ref>[https://eddiesextracts.com/extracts1700/pg1758_74.html Public Gazetteer extraction], 17 September 1768.</ref>

A Dublin Mercury extraction dated 22 December 1770 reports the death of Philip Glasco, junior, watchmaker in Christ Church Lane. It is retained as a report for the younger man, with the original issue still to be checked; it must not be substituted for the elder watchmaker’s reported 1772 death.<ref>[https://eddiesextracts.com/extracts1700/dm1723_73.html Dublin Mercury extraction], 22 December 1770.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Uphall household review, 23 October 2026 ===

The selected Scottish father hypothesis remains 18%. The 1711 record names Philip, not Mary; the unresolved question is whether that Scottish child became the elder Dublin watchmaker. The new 1701 and 1716 marriage evidence establishes Scottish households, not migration or this junior’s parentage.

Two Findmypast FamilySearch-derived entries name Philip Glasgow, male, baptised 3 June 1711 at Uphall, father Thomas Glasgow and mother Jean Duncan. They corroborate the maintained Scottish child account and do not identify a Mary. The older Mary label is an editorial inconsistency, not a second contemporary child. The separate family citation giving 21 October 1711/Linlithgow remains an unresolved index discrepancy: its underlying page was inaccessible and the present search did not find it. Duplicate transcriptions do not supply independent testimony. 72% is a subjective probable assessment of the complete existing father-profile pair, including the unproved identification of the 1675 child with the 1701 adult. It is not 99% merely because a transcript names a father Thomas. The alternative 21 October/Linlithgow citation remains unresolved. Philip’s Scottish child identity is the basis of this assessment; his later identification with the elder Dublin watchmaker remains uncertain and is not upgraded. No mother, parent selection, birth/death field or live WikiTree value changes. Original parish registers were not inspected.

The dated review above supersedes earlier statements that the 1701 marriage was only family information, that the 1711 child was Mary, or that the 1715 Edinburgh child supports the Uphall sequence. Other earlier evidence and unresolved alternatives remain below.

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1241]] is assessed at 18% (uncertain). The younger Dublin watchmaker shares the elder’s name, trade and address, but the selected father account is now labelled Mary and starts with conflicting 1711 Scottish entries. No source identifies that Scottish person as the elder Dublin father.

Complete selected father-profile proposition, with identity limits below.

Next useful test: Reconcile the 1711 Mary/Philip events and inspect Dublin apprenticeship/probate for an actual elder–younger parent clause; compare Glasco-146.

Source basis already held: [https://eddiesextracts.com/extracts1700/pg1758_74.html Public Gazetteer extracts, 1758–1774: Philip Glasco junior marriage]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ48-S7Z Philip at Uphall,3 June 1711: retained Thomas/Jean child index]; [https://eddiesextracts.com/extracts1700/dm1723_73.html Dublin Mercury extracts, 1723–1773: death of Philip Glasco junior]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.

=== Family and duplicate accounts ===
The current uncertain father [[Glasgow-1241|Philip Glasgow]] remains an unproved attachment to the elder watchmaker/Scottish-child account. ''Younger'', shared trade and address support the two-generation model, but the inspected marriage and wife-death notices name no parent. The Scottish 1711 baptism must not become this younger man’s own birth.

[[Glasco-147|Philip Glasco]] is a strong same-person match: its current structured spouse Teresa Plunkett agrees with the unusual name, younger designation, trade and address of these notices. Its estimated 1740 birth and quoted 1772 inventory/sonship claims need their own source verification. Retain both accounts for review; no live merge or duplicate spouse attachment has been performed. A 1772 grant date alone would not exclude a 1770 death.<ref>[https://www.virtualtreasury.ie/item/PROI-DKPRI-26-7 Dublin probate index], cited by the Glasco-147 profile; the quoted wording and precise grant role were not independently rechecked in this review.</ref>
